brief.headline: Push for a 2–3% price cut: they earn 8.5% net margin vs 4.8% peer median and are in safe financial health — there is clear headroom.

priceAsk.summary: Request a 2–3% reduction on rigid plastic packaging rates
priceAsk.target: Target saving of ₹0.50–0.75 L annually on our ₹26.17 L spend
priceAsk.basis: Triveni runs an 8.5% net margin, well above the 4.8% peer median — a 3.7 percentage-point cushion that proves room exists in their pricing structure

paymentTermAsk.summary: Tighten payment terms from 45 days to 30 days
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹2.15 L working capital freed; alternatively move to 30 days after receipt instead of current 45 days

brief.financialLeverage: Triveni earned ₹179.69 Cr revenue with an 8.5% net margin and 14.5% EBITDA margin in FY2024-25 — both comfortably above peer medians of 4.8% net and healthy enough to absorb modest price pressure. Zero debt (0.00x debt-to-equity) and 75.84x interest coverage signal balance-sheet strength. However, their 6.6% return on capital trails the 12.6% peer median, and negative free cash flow of ₹-6.59 Cr plus EPF payment delays hint at liquidity tightness despite profitability. We represent just 0.15% of their revenue (₹26.17 L of ₹179.69 Cr), so our leverage is low in isolation — we must compete them or bundle commitments to gain traction.

evidence.point: They earn a net margin nearly double the peer median
Strong EBITDA margin well above typical packaging converters
Our spend is a rounding error in their total revenue
They show signs of cash tightness despite healthy margins
evidence.figure: ₹-6.59 Cr free cash flow and EPF payment delays flagged

evidence.point: Return on capital lags peer median by nearly half

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue; pharma bottles, caps, and preforms — top second-source with B (65/100) health

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed ₹946.50 Cr leader in rigid pharma packaging (pails, containers, bottles) with A (79/100) health score — robust, credible alternate

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: ₹701.17 Cr listed player offering moulded and blow-moulded bottles and caps; C (57/100) health but broad capability match

risks: We are only 0.15% of their revenue — low standalone clout means they may not prioritize our ask unless we bundle volume or show credible alternate quotes
EPF payment delays and ₹-6.59 Cr negative free cash flow suggest liquidity stress; pushing too hard on price and terms simultaneously could strain continuity of supply
No borrowing-cost data or current internal pricing benchmarks available — our price ask rests solely on the margin gap, which they may defend as earned efficiency rather than excess
Their 102d receivables vs 45d payables means they run a 124d cash conversion cycle (vs 114d peer median) — accelerating our payment may help them but won't unlock large cash savings for us
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and we'd like to align pricing with the market — your 8.5% margin gives us confidence there's room to sharpen rates by 2–3% while still protecting your profitability.
